overview: The abilities packet is the server's flight permission broadcast: it carries allow-flight, invulnerable, creative, and the fly and walk speed factors, and it is the synchronization oracle anticheats use to validate the client's own abilities packet (C13). Checks pair the two directions: the server send sets the player's canFly and isFlying state, and the client send is checked against that state, so a flying flag without a server grant is a spoof. Grim runs a dedicated both-direction check plus a fly-flag spoof check; older anticheats fold the client abilities packet into their packet dispatch to feed movement physics.

checks.name: Abilities state sync (Grim)
checks.purpose: Keep the player's flight capability and flying flag in sync with what the server last sent on S39, so every other movement check reasons about the same flight state the client was granted.
checks.how_it_works: PacketPlayerAbilities listens on both directions. On the client abilities packet (C13) it sets player.isFlying to the packet's flying flag gated on player.canFly. On the server send (S39) it opens a transaction, remembers the last sent allow-flight value, and if flight was just revoked schedules a netty task that fires a setback when the client's transaction has not confirmed receipt within max-ping-out-of-flying (default 1000ms). A real-time task then applies canFly and isFlying from the server packet. The comment in the source explains the ordering hazard: Mojang's netcode lets ability packets arrive out of order, so state is applied one tick late to stop a client from flying for a tick before the anticheat knows.
checks.detects: Clients that fly while the server has not granted flight, and clients that keep flying after the server revokes the ability. This is the S39-side half of fly-cheat detection.
checks.variations: Artemis mirrors the server abilities packet into its emulated entity capabilities in EmulatorPreProcessor (GPacketPlayServerAbilities), and BetterAnticheat's PlayerCapabilities reads WrapperPlayServerPlayerAbilities into isFlying, canFly and flySpeed fields; both are the same S39-as-oracle pattern.

checks.name: Fly flag spoof (Grim BadPacketsI)
checks.purpose: Flag a client abilities packet that claims flying while the server has never granted flight on S39.
checks.how_it_works: A PreVia packet receive listener: when the packet type is PLAYER_ABILITIES, the wrapper reports isFlying true, and player.canFly is false, the check flags and cancels the packet. canFly is only ever true after the server sent allow-flight on S39, so this is a direct cross-check of the client's C13 claim against the S39 grant.
checks.detects: Spoofed flying flags, creative-fly hacks that send the flying bit without permission, and clients that desync their abilities state from the server.
checks.variations: AutoEye reads the same client packet in its netty channel handler and pushes the flying bit into the movement physics, so its fly checks run with the client's claimed flight state; Observer's Move check tracks a creativeFly boolean from C13PacketPlayerAbilities and exempts movement while it is set.

checks.name: Abilities dispatch (AutoEye)
checks.purpose: Route the client abilities packet into the movement physics state so fly and timer checks see the client's claimed flight mode.
checks.how_it_works: The channel handler switch matches PacketPlayInAbilities and writes the wrapper's flying bit into the player's physics state via setFlying. It is the C13-side counterpart to the S39 grant: AutoEye has no server-side abilities reader, so it trusts the client bit and lets the movement checks decide whether the resulting motion is possible.
checks.detects: Fly cheats that move with the flying flag set. The state feeds the movement check pipeline rather than flagging directly.
checks.variations: The dispatch pattern is shared by the 1.8 anticheat generation: the abilities packet is folded into per-player state, and flight permission is either trusted from the client or not tracked at all. Grim is the outlier that validates the claim against the server send.
